ai.description: *Chikila fulleri* is a slender, 20–30 cm caecilian with a uniform dark grey to brownish-purple body. It is distinguished by a blunt, shovel-shaped snout and the absence of a visible tail.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Chikila fulleri* is best distinguished from other Indian caecilians by its unique, distinctively pale or whitish snout tip, which contrasts sharply with its darker body.
ai.habitat: *Chikila fulleri* inhabits moist, tropical evergreen forests and agricultural areas in Northeast India, typically found in soft soil at altitudes between 100 and 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: *Chikila fulleri* exhibits unique maternal care, where the mother guards her eggs and allows her hatchlings to feed on her nutrient-rich skin until they are independent.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Chikila fulleri* is oviparous and exhibits maternal care, with females brooding a clutch of 15–30 eggs in underground nests during the monsoon season (June–August).
ai.distributionRemarks: *Chikila fulleri* is found in Northeast India, specifically across the states of Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Meghalaya, Nagaland, and Tripura, at low to moderate elevations.
ai.callDescription: The Kuttal Caecilian produces a faint, high-pitched, rhythmic clicking sound, typically emitted from within moist soil or leaf litter in its subterranean habitat.
